newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-BHP awarded four Timor Sea permits.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-BHP awarded four Timor Sea permits.

text.p: The Broken Hill Proprietary Co Ltd said on Monday that its BHP Petroleum unit had been awarded four oil exploration permits in the zone of co-operation region of the Timor Sea between Australia and Indonesia.
BHP said the first well in the new permits was likely to be drilled this financial year (June-May).
BHP said the production sharing contracts awarded by Indonesian and Australia cover 7,391 square km.
It said three of the blocks, awarded after applications closed on August 1, were ZOCA 95-15, 96-17, and 95-19.

BHP said it had 100 percent equity in the first two of these permits and a one third stake in the latter along with operator Shell Development (Australia) and Woodside Petroleum Ltd. BHP said it was also awarded a one third stake in ZOCA 96-20 with Shell and Woodside as equal partners.
BHP now has a stake in six Timor Gap blocks and described the region as one of its exploration focus areas.

BHP already has an interest in ZOCA 91-01 and 91-12, with the latter block containing the Elang and Kakatua oil discoveries as well as part of the Bayu/Undan gas and condensate discovery. It has a 42.417 percent stake in this block.
BHP said the agreement involving the latest blocks included plans for forward work which involved the acquisition of seismic and the drilling of an exploration well this financial year in ZOCA 95-19.
